title: AR-Order RL Post-Training Reduces Order Robustness in Diffusion Language Models

contributions.purpose: Test whether autoregressive-order RL post-training compromises the order robustness that distinguishes diffusion LMs from AR models.
contributions.mechanism: Compare LLaDA-8B-Instruct (diffusion base), LLaDA-Instruct-JustGRPO (AR-order RL trained), and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (AR anchor) via a robustness ratio r=Acc(AF)/Acc(CF) on ReasonOrderQA and GSM8K.
contributions.evaluation: JustGRPO reduces order robustness: robustness ratio drops 0.192 on ReasonOrderQA and 0.138 on GSM8K, both exceeding the 0.10 decision threshold.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that JustGRPO significantly reduces order robustness in diffusion LMs, with robustness ratio drops of 0.192 on ReasonOrderQA and 0.138 on GSM8K, both exceeding our decision threshold of 0.10.

contributions.purpose: Quantify how far AR-order RL shifts the model toward AR-style order dependence.
contributions.mechanism: Position JustGRPO's robustness profile between the diffusion base and the AR anchor.
contributions.evaluation: JustGRPO covers approximately 53% of the robustness gap between diffusion base and AR anchor, suggesting partial internalization of AR-style order dependence.
contributions.source_quote: We show that JustGRPO's robustness profile sits between the diffusion base and AR anchor, covering approximately 53% of the robustness gap, suggesting partial internalization of AR-style order dependence.

contributions.purpose: Localize where the robustness degradation occurs by problem difficulty.
contributions.evaluation: Degradation is concentrated at medium difficulty (D2-D3) requiring multi-step reasoning, while simple problems (D1) remain robust.
contributions.source_quote: We reveal that the degradation is concentrated at medium difficulty levels (D2-D3), where multi-step reasoning is required, while simple problems (D1) remain robust.

contributions.purpose: Characterize the cost of AR-order RL gains.
contributions.mechanism: Relate CoT-First accuracy improvement to loss of order flexibility.
contributions.evaluation: AR-order RL improves CoT-First accuracy by up to 19.6 percentage points but reduces order flexibility, revealing an accuracy-robustness trade-off.
contributions.source_quote: We identify a fundamental accuracy-robustness trade-off: AR-order RL training improves CoT-First accuracy by up to 19.6 percentage points but at the cost of reduced order flexibility.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We provide the first empirical investigation of this question.
JustGRPO (Ou et al., 2025) applies Group Relative Policy Optimization to diffusion models using left-to-right token-level rewards, achieving strong results on reasoning benchmarks.

Yu et al. (2026) introduced the ReasonOrderQA benchmark to measure order robustness... Our work investigates whether this AR-order bias in RL training compromises the order flexibility that distinguishes diffusion LMs from their autoregressive counterparts.

notes: NEGATIVE/trade-off characterization paper: main claim is that an existing method (JustGRPO, Ou et al. 2025) degrades order robustness; identifies an accuracy-robustness trade-off. Analysis study reusing JustGRPO and the ReasonOrderQA benchmark (Yu et al. 2026); proposes no new method.
